title: Gao · draft general number-field refinement at 4843/5000 (0.9686)
description: Refinement of Axiom Math's all-number-field proof from 31/32 to 4843/5000 = 0.9686, a potential improvement of 3/20000. The scope is Dedekind zeta and finite-order Hecke L-functions over every number field, at every height, with the original pole exclusions. The refinement changes the y scale from 151/400 to 943/2500 while retaining the contours, detector and frequency cutoffs; no new arithmetic estimate is claimed. Original research and mathematical judgments: Dean Cureton and Jesse Thorner; original proof generation and Lean formalization: AxiomProver at Axiom Math. Zhongpai Gao supplies the refinement, Dirichlet bridge and tracker port, with AI assistance. The original 5,508 support modules, thirty native refinement replacements and all dependency notices and full licenses are retained. Five new bridge modules construct the rational ray character, identify its ideal series with Mathlib's Dirichlet L-function, and transfer the genuine native Hecke endpoint to Candidate.bound. They cover modulus 1, odd and imprimitive characters and nonprincipal s = 1. These bridge modules passed isolated checks on tracker Lean 4.34.1 / Mathlib d13f23b using the three standard axioms. Three proof-preserving compatibility repairs affect the idele norm theorem, finite-algebra Jacobson theorem and Kummer additive-homomorphism projections. The Kummer subgroup definitions and radical fixedness theorem passed isolated checks on the tracker pins; its whole module and downstream proof remain unverified. Five Mathlib-only helper modules use compatible imports and passed complete isolated checks. All thirty native refinement modules remain exact after import relocation. Native whole-library compilation, whole-closure tracker replay, Comparator and independent-kernel admission remain pending; isolated checks do not certify the complete endpoint. This draft claims no independently verified record or improvement to the current Dirichlet numerical record. Mathlib, OpenAI/math, Tau Ceti, LeanPool and vendored class-field-theory attribution is retained. The original source date is 12 October; this refinement and bridge are dated 3 November 2026.
